items.followUp: A car moves with uniform acceleration. Its initial speed is 5 m/s, its acceleration is 2 m/s², and it moves for 4 s. Use the second equation of motion to find its displacement.

rubric.why: The derivation uses the speed–time graph to represent displacement.
rubric.description: Identifies displacement as the area under the speed–time graph.
rubric.how: State that the area under the speed–time graph gives displacement.

rubric.why: The area of the graph is a trapezium.
rubric.description: Writes the trapezium-area expression for displacement.

rubric.why: The first equation of motion is substituted into the graph-area expression.
rubric.description: Uses v = u + at in the displacement expression.
rubric.how: Substitute v = u + at into s = ½(u + v)t.

rubric.why: This is the required derived equation.
rubric.description: Obtains the second equation of motion.

modelAnswer: For uniform acceleration, displacement s is the area under the speed–time graph.
The graph forms a trapezium, so s = ½(u + v)t.
From the first equation of motion, v = u + at.
Substituting, s = ½(u + u + at)t.
Therefore, s = ut + ½at², the second equation of motion.

items.followUp: Define potential energy and derive the expression for the gravitational potential energy of an object raised through height h.

rubric.why: The definition must connect kinetic energy with an object's motion.
rubric.description: Defines kinetic energy as the energy possessed due to motion.
rubric.how: State that kinetic energy is the energy an object possesses because of its motion.

rubric.why: The derivation begins with work done and Newton's second law.
rubric.description: Uses W = Fs and F = ma.
rubric.how: Write W = Fs and F = ma.

rubric.why: The motion relation connects work done with the change in speed.
rubric.description: Uses v² − u² = 2as to express the work done.
rubric.how: Substitute F = ma and as = (v² − u²)/2 into W = Fs.

rubric.why: Starting from rest gives the standard kinetic-energy expression.
rubric.description: Sets the initial speed to zero and obtains the kinetic-energy equation.
rubric.how: For u = 0, write KE = W = ½mv².

modelAnswer: Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by an object due to its motion.
The work done to give an object speed v from rest is W = Fs.
Using F = ma and v² − u² = 2as, W = mas = ½m(v² − u²).
For an object starting from rest, u = 0; therefore, KE = W = ½mv².

items.followUp: A steering wheel has a radius of 20 cm. Equal and opposite forces of 12 N act tangentially on opposite sides. Find the torque of the couple.

rubric.why: The radius must be converted to SI units and the perpendicular separation of the forces is the diameter.
rubric.description: Converts the radius and finds the couple arm as 0.32 m.
rubric.how: Convert 16 cm to 0.16 m, then calculate d = 2r = 0.32 m.

rubric.why: Torque of a couple is one force multiplied by the perpendicular distance between the forces.
rubric.description: Applies the torque-of-a-couple relation and substitutes the couple arm.
rubric.how: Write τ = Fd = F × 0.32 m = 0.32F N·m.

rubric.why: The question does not give the force magnitude needed for a numerical torque.
rubric.description: Notes that the torque cannot be calculated numerically without the force magnitude.
rubric.how: State that τ = 0.32F N·m and that a force value is required for a numerical answer.

modelAnswer: Given radius r = 16 cm = 0.16 m.
For two equal and opposite tangential forces, the couple arm is the diameter: d = 2r = 0.32 m.
Torque of a couple, τ = Fd.
Therefore, τ = F × 0.32 m = 0.32F N·m, where F is the magnitude of either force.
The force magnitude is not given, so a numerical value for the torque cannot be found.

items.followUp: Derive the expression for pressure at depth h in a liquid, and state what happens to pressure if the depth is doubled.

rubric.why: The derivation begins with the definition of pressure.
rubric.description: Writes pressure as force per unit area.

rubric.why: The mass of the liquid column is found from its density and volume.
rubric.description: Expresses the column volume and mass in terms of A and h.
rubric.how: Write V = Ah and m = ρV.

rubric.why: The liquid exerts a force equal to the weight of the column.
rubric.description: Uses the liquid column's weight as the force on the area.

rubric.why: Substitution and cancellation give the required pressure formula.
rubric.how: Substitute F = ρAhg into P = F/A and simplify.

modelAnswer: Pressure in a liquid is the force per unit area exerted by the liquid: P = F/A.
For a liquid column of depth h and cross-sectional area A, its volume is V = Ah.
Its mass is m = ρV = ρAh, so its weight is F = mg = ρAhg.
Therefore, P = F/A = ρAhg/A = ρgh.

items.followUp: Estimate the number of seconds in one week, showing the conversion from days to seconds.

rubric.why: Credit for converting one day from hours to seconds.
rubric.description: Uses 24 hours, 60 minutes per hour, and 60 seconds per minute.

rubric.why: The answer should state the seconds in a day and give a suitable estimate.

modelAnswer: 1 day = 24 h × 60 min/h × 60 s/min.
1 day = 86,400 s ≈ 8.64 × 10⁴ s, or approximately 10⁵ s.
